meta.title: Developers: webhook, Payload and signature
meta.description: How Vink sends approved document data to your system: the JSON envelope, HMAC-SHA256 signature checks, retries, test-send, and guides for Make, n8n, Zapier and Power Automate.

og.title: One signed webhook. Clean JSON, keyed by your own Fields.
og.alt: Vink for developers. One signed webhook with clean JSON, keyed by your own Fields.

header.title: One signed webhook. Clean JSON, keyed by your own Fields.
header.subtitle: When a Document is approved, Vink sends its data to your endpoint as one JSON POST. This page is everything you need to build the receiver.

overview.title: Overview
overview.p1: An Integration is an HTTPS endpoint you add in Vink and attach to one or more Forms. When a Document of that Form is approved, by a person or by Auto-Send, Vink sends one Delivery to each attached Integration.
overview.p2: The body is the Payload: the Document's values keyed by the Form's own Fields, inside a small envelope. Every request is signed, so your receiver can check that Vink sent it.

facts.signed: Signed with HMAC-SHA256 in the X-Vink-Signature header
facts.retries: Retried for about 8 hours on timeouts, 408, 429 and 5xx

overview.reading: Vink reads PDFs with Gemini on Vertex AI, EU region.
overview.apiReference: Calling Vink from your own code? The <link>API reference</link> describes the public API and its API Keys.
overview.inbound: Documents come in through the app today: upload several PDFs at once, or email them in. No code? Point any system's email at the Form's Intake Address, and each PDF attachment becomes a Document. There is no upload API yet. Need one? <link>Tell us</link>.

platforms.title: Make, n8n, Zapier and Power Automate
platforms.intro: No developer? These four automation platforms can receive the Webhook today. Vink sends the approved data, and you build the rest of the flow there: a row in a spreadsheet, a message to your team, a record in your accounting package.
platforms.listLabel: Automation platforms that work with Vink today
platforms.howTitle: How it works, on every platform
platforms.how: You make a receiving URL in the platform. In Vink, you paste it into a new Integration and attach that Integration to a Form. A test-send shows the platform your Fields, so you can map them to the next step. From then on, every approved Document of that Form goes there.
platforms.testFlag: A test-send carries "test": true. Before a step that writes real data, add a filter that only lets test = false through. Then tests never end up in your books.
platforms.secret: The URL is the key. These platforms can't easily check the X-Vink-Signature header, so anyone who has the URL can send data to it. Keep the URL out of emails, tickets and screenshots. If it leaks, make a new URL in the platform and paste it into the Integration in Vink.

make.title: Make
make.plan: Plan: works on Make's free plan (1,000 credits a month, 2 active scenarios). The Webhooks app is part of every plan, and a webhook starts the scenario right away.

steps.hook: In Make, create a scenario. Add the Webhooks app with the trigger Custom webhook. Choose Add, give the webhook a name and save. Copy the address Make shows.
steps.vink: In Vink, open Integrations and choose New Integration. Paste the address as the Endpoint URL and choose Create Integration. Then choose Attach to a Form.
steps.test: Make now waits for data. In Vink, choose Send test, pick the Form and Example values. Make learns your Fields from this test.
steps.map: Add the next module, for example Google Sheets, and map the values. They are under data, keyed by your own Field keys. Turn the scenario on.
steps.change: Changed the Form's Fields later? Open the webhook module, choose Detect new values and send another test.

make.lists: List Fields: a List Field arrives as an array, one object per entry. To handle each entry, for example one spreadsheet row per invoice line, put an Iterator on that array before the next module.
make.security: Extra lock: Make can check an API key. Add one to the webhook in Make. In Vink, add the header x-make-apikey with that key to the Integration, and mark it Secret. Now the URL alone is not enough.
make.note: Make answers 200 at once and queues the data. If the webhook's queue is full, Make answers 400: Vink then marks the Delivery failed, and an Admin can send it again from the Document.

n8n.title: n8n
n8n.plan: Plan: free when you host n8n yourself (Community Edition). n8n Cloud is paid, with a free trial.

steps.hook: In n8n, make a workflow with the Webhook node as its trigger. Set HTTP Method to POST and leave Respond on Immediately. Copy the Test URL.
steps.vink: In Vink, open Integrations and choose New Integration. Paste the Test URL as the Endpoint URL and choose Create Integration. Then choose Attach to a Form.
steps.test: In n8n, choose Listen for test event. In Vink, choose Send test, pick the Form and Example values. The test shows up in n8n, with your values under body.data.
steps.map: Add the next nodes and map the values.
steps.live: Publish the workflow and copy the Production URL. Edit the Integration in Vink and replace the Test URL with it. The Test URL only works while n8n is listening for a test.

n8n.lists: List Fields: a List Field arrives as an array, one object per entry. A Split Out node on that array, for example body.data.lines, makes one item per entry.
n8n.security: Extra lock: n8n can check a header. Set the Webhook node's Authentication to Header Auth with a name and a long random value. In Vink, add the same header to the Integration and mark it Secret.
n8n.note: n8n Cloud and a self-hosted n8n behave the same here. A self-hosted n8n must be reachable over HTTPS from the internet.

zapier.title: Zapier
zapier.plan: Plan: needs a paid Zapier plan. Webhooks by Zapier is not part of the free plan.

steps.hook: In Zapier, make a Zap. As the trigger, choose Webhooks by Zapier with the event Catch Hook. Copy the webhook URL Zapier shows.
steps.vink: In Vink, open Integrations and choose New Integration. Paste the URL as the Endpoint URL and choose Create Integration. Then choose Attach to a Form.
steps.test: In Vink, choose Send test, pick the Form and Example values. In Zapier, choose Test trigger and pick the request that came in.
steps.map: Add the action, for example Google Sheets, and map the values from data. Publish the Zap.

zapier.lists: List Fields: a List Field arrives as an array of objects. Zapier shows its entries as line items: an action that supports line items takes them all at once. For one action per entry, use Looping by Zapier.
zapier.security: Lock: a Catch Hook doesn't check headers, so the secret URL is the only lock. Treat it like a password.
zapier.note: A Zap that is off or deleted answers 404 after a while. Vink then marks the Delivery failed. Turn the Zap on, and an Admin sends the failed Delivery again from the Document.

powerAutomate.title: Power Automate
powerAutomate.plan: Plan: needs a Premium licence. The trigger When an HTTP request is received is a Premium trigger.

steps.hook: In Power Automate, make a cloud flow that starts with the trigger When an HTTP request is received. If the trigger shows Who can trigger the flow?, set it to Anyone. The other options only let in signed-in users from your own tenant, so they refuse Vink.
steps.url: Save the flow. The trigger now shows the HTTP URL. Copy it.
steps.vink: In Vink, open Integrations and choose New Integration. Paste the URL as the Endpoint URL and choose Create Integration. Then choose Attach to a Form.
steps.test: In Vink, choose Send test, pick the Form and Example values. In the flow's run history, open that run and copy the body of the trigger's output.
steps.schema: In the trigger, choose Use sample payload to generate schema and paste that body. Your Fields now show up as dynamic content.
steps.map: Add the next actions, map the values from data and save.

powerAutomate.lists: List Fields: a List Field arrives as an array. Apply to each on that array runs the next actions once per entry.
powerAutomate.security: Lock: the URL contains a signature (sig=) that works like a password. Anyone who has the full URL can start the flow. If it leaks, make a new URL in Power Automate and paste it into the Integration.
powerAutomate.note: Power Automate answers 202 at once, which counts as delivered in Vink.

envelope.title: Envelope
envelope.intro: This is a real Payload from a demo Form called Invoices, with a List Field for the invoice lines. The keys under data are your own Field keys, so every Form has its own shape.

rules.title: Three rules your parser can rely on
rules.present: Every key is always present, including optional Fields.

table.delivery_id: Unique per Delivery. It stays the same when a Delivery is retried or sent again, so use it to deduplicate.
table.test: true for a test-send, false for a real Delivery.
table.document: The Document's id, its file name and when it was uploaded (ISO 8601, UTC).
table.form: The Form's id and the Form Version the Document was read with.
table.approval: manual or auto (Auto-Send), the approving user's id (null for Auto-Send) and when it was approved.
table.data: The values, keyed by Field. Numbers are numbers, dates are YYYY-MM-DD, yes/no Fields are booleans and Lists are arrays of objects.

signature.title: Verify the signature
signature.intro: Each request carries a header with a timestamp and an HMAC-SHA256 signature. Every Integration has its own secret, starting with whsec_. You find it on the Integration in the app.

steps.title: To verify a request
steps.parse: Split the header on commas and read t (Unix seconds) and v1 (hex).
steps.sign: Compute HMAC-SHA256 with your secret over the string '{t}.{rawBody}': the timestamp, a dot, and the raw request body exactly as received.
steps.compare: Compare your result with v1 using a constant-time comparison.
steps.time: Reject the request if t is more than 5 minutes away from your clock. This stops a captured request from being replayed.

signature.raw: Use the raw body bytes. Parsing and re-serialising the JSON changes whitespace and key order, and the signature no longer matches.

delivery.title: Delivery and retries
delivery.intro: Vink waits up to 15 seconds for your answer.

table.retryResult: Tried again after about 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours and 6 hours: 6 attempts over roughly 8 hours.
table.failResult: Failed right away. An Admin can send a failed Delivery again from the app.

delivery.retryAfter: A Retry-After header (seconds or an HTTP date) is honoured, up to 24 hours.
delivery.redirects: Redirects are not followed. Your endpoint must use HTTPS.
delivery.atLeastOnce: Delivery is at-least-once. The same Delivery can arrive twice, for example when your receiver saved it but timed out before answering. Store delivery_id and skip one you have already handled.
delivery.headers: You can add your own headers to an Integration, such as an API key or Basic auth. Mark a header as secret and its value is stored encrypted and only shown masked afterwards. Vink sets Content-Type and X-Vink-Signature itself.
delivery.screenshot: A Document's Delivery status in Vink, showing a retry

testSend.title: Test-send
testSend.body: From an Integration, send a test to your endpoint before any real Document goes out. Choose example values for every Field, or empty values so your receiver sees null and []. You can also send an approved Document again as a test.
testSend.flag: A test carries "test": true, is signed like a real one and is never a Delivery: it isn't retried and doesn't appear in a Document's Delivery log. The answer from your endpoint is shown right away.
testSend.screenshot: An Integration in Vink with the result of a test-send

service.title: Integration service
service.lead: No developer, or no time? We build the connection for you.
service.body: A one-off build, never part of a plan. We write the receiver that takes the Payload into your system, whether that is an ERP, an accounting package, a spreadsheet or a database, and sets up your Forms with you.

includes.title: What you get
includes.receiver: A receiver that verifies the signature and writes the data into your system
includes.forms: Your Forms and Fields set up with you, tested on your own documents
includes.hosting: You host it, or we host it for a monthly fee on request
includes.changes: Maintenance and changes later, billed per job

need.title: What we need from you
need.system: Which system the data should land in, and access to a test environment
need.contact: One person who knows how the data is used

service.priceNote: A fixed price, agreed before we start.
